Week 4 · Capacity planning

California Capacity Expansion

CAISO planning benchmarks using observed 2025 demand.

Greenfield benchmark

The gas-only benchmark includes CCGT and frame CT. The renewable extension adds utility PV and onshore wind.

Key findings

    Renewable builds face published planning ceilings. Net costs deduct production credits on electricity generated. Modeled shortfalls are scenario outputs and do not describe 2025 outages.

    Detailed results

    Study definition

    Hypothetical CAISO greenfield planning benchmarks. The renewable case is a mixed-year benchmark using 2025 demand, 2026 candidate availability and 2022 weather.

    Geography
    CAISO balancing authority. Results apply to the modeled CAISO boundary and do not cover all California or individual CCAs.
    Demand and trade
    Observed 2025 hourly EMS load and fixed observed signed CAISO net interchange.
    Renewable inputs
    Published 2022 RESOLVE weather profiles and 2026 candidate availability and eligibility. Existing-fleet dispatch is outside both greenfield cases.
    Costs
    CPUC Draft 2025 I&A Mid in real 2022 USD. Assumed NSE penalty is $10,000/MWh. Border settlements and additional carbon charges are outside the objective.

    The cases describe hypothetical investments. They do not establish historical construction or an official procurement plan.

    Input explorer

    Demand is observed in 2025. Candidate factors are published 2022 weather profiles, shown at their mapped 2025 study hours.

    Utility PV availability · %
    Onshore wind availability · %

    Candidate inputs

    Published annual fixed coefficients were used directly. Credits are shown as deductions per MWh generated.

    Sources and methodology

    Measured · 2025
    CAISO monthly historical EMS workbooks (July workbook) and the CAISO production and net interchange workbook.
    Planning · 2022 weather / 2026 availability
    Published CPUC RESOLVE inputs and companion workbooks.
    Planning · Draft Mid
    CPUC draft resource cost workbook, 2025 cost vintage in real 2022 USD.
    Time mapping and qualifications

    Study intervals run from January 1, 2025 00:00 Pacific through January 1, 2026 00:00 Pacific. The charts use hourly interval starts with UTC and Pacific offsets. For modeled weather, match the same month, day and hour using fixed Pacific standard time (UTC−08:00). Solar timing supported that assumption empirically. Wind’s UTC offset remains independently unverified.

    Keep the published area/profile links and AC solar factors. Builds respect the benchmark’s site, area, technology and linked shared build limits. Contract minimums do not impose builds in this greenfield study. Fixed historical boundary flows do not respond to candidate decisions. Credit deductions apply to actual modeled renewable generation.

    Validation

    Solver status applies to the specified model and constraints.

    Residuals and tolerances

    Brownfield

    Not solved — insufficient reconciled existing-system inputs.

    The existing fleet is incompletely reconciled. Storage, load and hybrid accounting is unresolved. The elective-retirement envelope is unverified.

    Technical blockers

    The matched inventory covers only part of CAISO gas capability. The available signed battery telemetry has unresolved fall-back intervals and does not resolve charging, pumping, hybrid components or specified-import accounting against EMS. Physical capability and local-area tags do not establish permission to retire units. Missing results remain unavailable.
